body:
> One of the methods that Psalm reports an error for doesn't throw an exception on its own, rather a method it calls throws one which then bubbles up through the call stack.

So effectively it throws.The main goal of `checkForThrowsDocblock` it to find unhandled exceptions - and  psalm tells you you may get exception running this method, because you don't handle it there. `@throws` is supposed to be specified for all methods up to the point where it's handled.
You're right, but still I'm not sure why the `@psalm-suppress` annotation isn't working here.

Can you elaborate on why you want to suppress it? Does psalm identify exception as thrown where it really isn't, or does it fail to see you actually handle that exception? Or is there any other reason?

I added a `@throws` annotation to the method earlier, but from my understanding of how `@psalm-suppress` is supposed to work, this could potentially be a bug. I'm not interested in getting this instance to work so much as I am curious why the annotation didn't in the first place.
If this was made to work, it would be great to be able to ignore specific exceptions in specific methods.
@weirdan `@psalm-suppress MissingThrowsDocblock Throwable` turns off all the things?
Yeah, but I was thinking about suppressing more specific kinds of exceptions.
Would support for `@template T as Throwable` + `@psalm-suppress MissingThrowsDocblock T` be overkill ?
p.s. I can see `@psalm-suppress MissingThrowsDocblock TypeError` being useful for libraries that support environments where `TypeError` doesn't exist :)

> Would support for `@template T as Throwable` + `@psalm-suppress MissingThrowsDocblock T` be overkill ?

I don't see a practical application for that, so I would say yes.

@SignpostMarv but that would mean function call affects outer (callee) scope. Generally, all of the test methods should be treated as if all exceptions are suppressed - because PHPUnit would catch and handle everything that's thrown.

issue.title: Edit profile features

repository.name: brewmap
repository.description: Laravel-based application for brewery tourism social media platform.

issue.body:
As an authenticated user I would like to:

- [x] change my public name
- [x] change my password (with previous password confirmation)
- [x] change my email (with confirmation)
- [x] change other stuff in profile (description, avatar, things like this)

To discuss: "Edit profile" page fields should be asynchronous, eg. changing values in inputs should automatically save them in database. I would see it as forms in Blade files on one `/profile/edit` page and some calls to API within.
